papers.title: Impact of improved access to medications for opioid use disorder in residential treatment
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Health officials in the United States (USA) are seeking strategies to mitigate overdose mortality. Medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) are effective but underused in residential treatment centers. We used a simulation model to investigate population-level health and health economic impacts of requiring residential treatment centers to offer MOUD to patients with opioid use disorder (OUD). papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Drug use among United States military veterans has clinical and public health implications. This study determined the risk of post-military service drug overdose mortality (1979-2021) among all veterans who served in the military during the 1961-1975 Vietnam War-era. DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study compared the risk of drug overdose mortality among all United States military veterans that served in Vietnam during the Vietnam War (theater veterans) to that of all veterans who served during the Vietnam War but not in Vietnam (non-theater). This comprehensive population assessment included veterans born between 1900 and 1958, alive as of 1979 and with military service between 1961 and 1975. papers.title: Early patient-reported outcomes and planned persistence with lenacapavir for HIV preexposure prophylaxis in routine clinical care
papers.abstract: This multicenter study evaluated early patient-reported outcomes (PROs) among individuals initiating twice-yearly lenacapavir (LEN) for HIV preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) in routine care. Convenience, driven by reduced dosing frequency, was the primary motivation for LEN initiation, and overall satisfaction was high despite frequent but generally mild injection-site reactions. Persistent nodules and pain emerged as the leading patient-reported concerns regarding future continuation, highlighting the importance of patient-centered counseling and implementation strategies to optimize long-term persistence with long-acting PrEP.

papers.title: Comorbidity burden and outcomes with long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine in the RELATIVITY cohort
papers.abstract: In RELATIVITY, among 3118 virologically suppressed people with HIV switching to long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine, 40.0% had at least one comorbidity and 16.8% had multimorbidity. Higher comorbidity burden identified older, clinically complex participants with longer ART exposure, lower CD4 nadir, and more prior AIDS. Virological failure (0.6-0.8%), definitive discontinuation (4.3-6.3%), and complete injection coverage, defined as proportion of days covered (PDC) of 100% (83.4-87.2%) were similar across strata, suggesting that comorbidity burden alone should not preclude individualized use in routine care.

papers.title: Predicting persistent fever in patients with cancer receiving antibiotics: a machine learning approach
papers.abstract: Persistent fever after initiating intravenous antibiotics is common in hospitalized patients with cancer and often leads to additional imaging and antimicrobial escalation. Early identification of patients unlikely to remain febrile could provide additional information during clinical reassessment. We developed and externally validated machine learning models to predict persistent fever 48-72 h after antibiotic initiation using electronic health records from two academic hospitals. Adult cancer patients with fever within 24-48 h of treatment were included. Models incorporated demographics, comorbidities, laboratory results, vital signs, and temperature patterns. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Streptococcus pneumoniae (Spn) infections are preceded by nasal colonization. By conferring protection against nasopharyngeal carriage, pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have reduced the global incidence of disease. papers.title: Povorcitinib for nonsegmental vitiligo: two randomized, controlled, phase 3 STOP-V trials
papers.abstract: There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. Here, 52-week primary results are reported from two parallel phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of once-daily povorcitinib (oral, highly selective JAK1 inhibitor) 30 mg in adults with moderate-to-severe NSV (STOP-V1 and STOP-V2). STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 enrolled 467 and 449 patients, respectively. In both studies, the primary endpoint of ≥75% improvement in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI75) at week 52 was met, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful repigmentation with povorcitinib versus placebo (STOP-V1: 18.9% versus 6.8%; odds ratio, 3.1; 95% confidence interval 1.6-5.9; P = 0.0003; STOP-V2: 18.9% versus 3.1%; odds ratio, 7.5; 95% confidence interval 3.0-18.6; P < 0.0001). papers.title: Global, regional and national burden of cervical cancer in 1990-2023 with forecasts to 2050: a Global Burden of Disease study
papers.abstract: Although highly preventable, cervical cancer remains one of the most common malignancies among women worldwide. As part of the Global Burden of Disease study, we estimated cervical cancer incidence, mortality and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. In 2023, 887,000 new cases (95% uncertainty interval 682,000-1,170,000), 369,000 deaths (292,000-475,000) and 13.3 million DALYs (10.1-17.4) were estimated globally. Age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) were more than four and seven times higher in low- versus high-income countries. Between 1990 and 2023, global ASIR was largely stable (-0.4% (-26.6 to 34.7)), whereas ASMR changed by -17.5% (-36.2 to 13.4). papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: While evidence on the individual effects of prenatal cannabis and tobacco exposure on offspring cognition is accumulating, their combined impact remains understudied. Therefore, we examined the interaction between prenatal cannabis and tobacco exposure on fluid (e.g. reasoning abilities) and crystallized (e.g. acquired knowledge) cognition in middle childhood. We also compared cognition in children with prenatal co-exposure to those with cannabis-only exposure, tobacco-only exposure and no exposure. DESIGN: Cross-sectional exploratory analysis of baseline data from an ongoing longitudinal cohort study. SETTING: Data collected between 2016 and 2018 from the United States-based Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study were extracted. papers.title: Measles
papers.abstract: Measles is reemerging, with cases and outbreaks increasing across the United States and other countries where measles had previously been eliminated. Most U.S. physicians have no experience with treating measles. However, the increasing likelihood of encountering not only children but also adults with measles requires a clinical review of the epidemiology, prevention, diagnosis, and management of this previously uncommon infection for general internal medicine physicians and hospitalists who care for adults in settings with measles reemergence. Prompt clinical suspicion, infection control measures, and notification of public health departments support timely diagnosis and disease control.

papers.abstract: Recruiting participants for clinical trials is a challenge, often limited by inefficient methods for identifying eligible candidates. Clinical trial recruitment support systems (CTRSS) can enhance recruitment efficiency by leveraging data from electronic health records (EHR). We evaluated two CTRSS-recruIT and KAS+-to quantify their real-world impact on enrollment. papers.abstract: Sleep is essential for health, yet studying its dynamics requires manual sleep staging, a labor-intensive step in research and clinical care. Across centers, polysomnography (PSG) recordings are traditionally scored in 30-s epochs for pragmatic, not physiological, reasons and vary in electrode count, montage, and subject characteristics. These constraints challenge harmonized multi-center studies and the discovery of robust biomarkers on shorter timescales. papers.title: Implementation strategies for digital relapse prevention in schizophrenia identified during a randomized controlled trial
papers.abstract: Digital mental health technologies hold promise, yet their integration into routine care remains challenging. This study reports findings from an implementation workshop conducted midway through an ongoing multi-site randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating a smartphone-based relapse prevention app for patients with schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder. Sixteen stakeholders, including developers, researchers, and clinicians, discussed experiences and barriers using a semi-structured agenda, incorporating prior feedback from three focus groups with people with lived experience, and analyzed the discussions using an adopted R(E)-AIM framework (Reach, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance). papers.title: Characterizing cognitive concerns in subjective cognitive decline using large language models and electronic health record notes
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) refers to self- or informant-reported cognitive concerns despite normal objective testing. These concerns are often documented as free text in electronic health records (EHRs), limiting systematic analysis. We characterized cognitive concern domains and assessed differences across demographic subgroups. METHODS: We studied 2175 individuals aged ≥65 years with an EHR-derived SCD phenotype. Using large language models with expert review, we derived a taxonomy of concern themes and sub-themes and assigned themes to note excerpts. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis survivors face increased long-term cognitive risk, but contemporary U.S. population-level estimates of claims-ascertained dementia remain limited. papers.abstract: Although modern machine-learning models attain strong predictive performance, their clinical adoption remains limited by a lack of transparency. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood diarrhoeal disease remains a leading cause of child mortality worldwide. Although predictive models have been increasingly proposed for early warning, their methodological quality and validation have not been systematically appraised using formal risk of bias frameworks. This systematic review aimed to identify, describe, and critically appraise individual-level prediction models and population-level forecasting studies for childhood diarrhoeal outcomes, focusing on model development, validation, reporting quality, and operational readiness. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The inherent biological heterogeneity of tumors continues to pose a challenge for achieving accurate survival status prediction in breast cancer. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) serostatus disclosure to sexual partners is essential for effective HIV management among women of reproductive age. However, nationally representative evidence from Lesotho is lacking. Therefore, this study assessed the prevalence and factors associated with HIV serostatus disclosure using the Lesotho Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) (2023-2024). METHODS: The study used the most recent Lesotho DHS 2023-2024 dataset. Data were analyzed using STATA version 18, and a logistic regression model was fitted. papers.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Digital devices play an increasingly important role in the detection and screening of cardiac arrhythmias. Atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common arrhythmia, is associated with an increased risk of stroke, heart failure, and mortality. This review summarises the current evidence on wearable devices for screening and diagnosing atrial fibrillation. papers.abstract: Tuberculosis is the deadliest infectious disease, and treatments for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis are lengthy and toxic. By analyzing a large international database (N = 7,750), we identified patient risk phenotypes linked to unfavorable outcomes. papers.title: Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer
papers.abstract: Quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) provides a mechanistic framework for integrating biological and pharmacological knowledge in drug development. Simultaneously, advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in multi-modal data analysis, are transforming how biological information is derived. I argue that AI should not be viewed as a data integration tool, but as a new layer of quantitative measurement generation. This reframing positions QSP as a foundational model of biology, used here in a conceptual rather than technical sense, and AI as a source of quantitative inputs.

papers.title: Understanding barriers to HIV testing during pregnancy among women who attended ANC in Soweto, Johannesburg: a socio-ecological perspective
papers.abstract: Vertical transmission of HIV remains a significant challenge to maternal and child health in high burden settings. Early identification of maternal HIV status enables timely antiretroviral therapy initiation and helps prevent transmission during pregnancy, childbirth, and breastfeeding. This study explored barriers to HIV testing uptake among pregnant and postpartum women attending antenatal care (ANC) services in Soweto, Johannesburg. A qualitative research design was employed, involving in-depth interviews with ten adult women who accessed ANC services. Data were analysed thematically using Atlas.ti 23 software. papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Opioid use disorder (OUD) remains a major public health challenge that disproportionately impacts Veterans, 34% of whom live rurally. papers.abstract: Clinical AI governance has advanced rapidly in technical validation, regulatory compliance, risk management, human oversight, and postdeployment monitoring. We present Medotor, a locally deployed system for screening patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) for biologic therapy, and evaluate prompt design on 163 retrospective cases (132 eligible and 31 ineligible). papers.title: Engagement-Supportive Mechanisms in Stress-Focused Digital Mental Health Interventions With Adaptive, Conversational, and Context-Aware Systems: Narrative Review
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Stress is a widespread public health concern associated with cardiovascular disease, depression, anxiety, and reduced quality of life. Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs), delivered through smartphones, web platforms, and wearables, offer scalable support for stress management but often struggle to sustain user engagement. Evidence describing how adaptive, conversational, and context-aware mechanisms function together within stress-focused DMHIs remains fragmented. OBJECTIVE: This review aims to synthesize evidence on engagement-supportive mechanisms in stress-focused DMHIs, with attention to personalization; biometric feedback; just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs); gamification; AI, including large language models (LLMs); and methodological approaches to studying engagement. papers.title: Erlotinib in a once-daily high-dose oral regimen could mitigate Chikungunya virus titer in mice
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a re-emerging arbovirus that causes debilitating inflammatory arthritis, for which no approved antiviral therapy currently exists. This study investigated the potential of repurposing erlotinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, as an anti-CHIKV agent. Erlotinib demonstrated promising in vitro antiviral activity, with EC50 values in the low micromolar range and a favorable selectivity index. However, in vivo evaluation in C57BL/6 mice revealed pharmacokinetic limitations, characterized by rapid absorption and clearance, resulting in insufficient drug exposure under standard dosing regimens. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Drug overdose is a leading cause of death among people released from correctional facilities, and the risk of overdose is higher among people living with HIV (PLWH). Overdose remains understudied in people in South Africa despite the high burden of HIV and hazardous opioid use. The researchers aimed to qualitatively explore how formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and OUD in South Africa understand, experience, and respond to overdose. METHODS: People with HIV and self-reported hazardous opioid use prior to correctional facility release or shortly after release were enrolled in a convenience sample. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Acute psychotic episodes in schizophrenia represent a critical stage in clinical management, often characterized by significant ideobehavioral disorganization, poor therapeutic adherence, and increased suicide risk. Currently, a broad consensus of clinicians and experts consider long-acting injectables (LAIs) a valuable and indispensable tool in clinical practice, also used as a first-line treatment in the acute phases of the illness. papers.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Delirium is a state of acute confusion characterized by deficits in attention that occurs commonly during hospitalization and is associated with adverse outcomes; however, the association of delirium with longitudinal cognitive trajectories is not fully understood. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of delirium during hospitalization with subsequent development of mild cognitive impairment (MCI), dementia, and longitudinal cognitive trajectories. papers.title: Pre-treatment machine learning prediction of local failure and time to local failure after Gamma Knife radiosurgery for radioresistant brain metastases
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Local control after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for radioresistant brain metastases remains variable. Melanoma and renal cell carcinoma brain metastases are relatively radioresistant, yet pre-treatment prediction of local failure and its timing remains limited. We developed and internally validated a survival machine learning model to predict lesion-specific local failure and time to local failure using only pre-GKRS variables. papers.title: AI Literacy as a Leadership Competency: Preparing Nurse Executives for Artificial Intelligence Governance
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly integrating into health care delivery, influencing clinical, operational, and strategic decision-making. Nurse executives must therefore possess competencies that enable informed oversight of AI-enabled systems. This article proposes an AI literacy competency framework for nurse executive practice, adapted from existing AI literacy scholarship and aligned with nursing leadership responsibilities. The framework provides a conceptual foundation for integrating AI literacy into leadership competency development, translating theoretical constructs into practice that is aligned with executive decision-making. papers.title: AI-Assisted Analysis of Clinical Trials to Identify Failed Drugs for Revival via Drug Delivery Technologies
papers.abstract: Numerous drug candidates showed great promise in experimental and preclinical investigations but failed in clinical trials. One cause to this problem may be nonspecific drug biodistribution, leading to adverse effects in healthy organs. Drug delivery technologies are developed to overcome this exact problem by navigating drugs more selectively to the disease sites. Therefore, they hold the promise to revive at least some failed drugs. However, it is challenging to identify such candidates revivable by drug delivery: first, there lacks systemic survey and documentation of drug biodistribution in patients during the trials; second, clinical trial results, especially the failed ones, are often reported in unstructured and/or inconsistent language. Here, we harnessed the recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) agents and large language models (LLMs) to tackle with the second problem.

papers.title: Attitudes of people living with dementia and their carers towards the use of generative artificial intelligence to inform structured medication reviews
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Polypharmacy is common in people living with dementia (PLwD) and associated with adverse outcomes. Although Structured Medication Reviews (SMRs) are recommended to optimise medication regimens, their delivery is often constrained by limited resources. Artificial intelligence (AI) may support SMRs, yet little is known about how it is perceived by PLwD and their carers. This study explored their experiences of polypharmacy, views on SMRs and attitudes towards use of AI tools in SMRs. METHODS: Semi-structured interviews with 12 PLwD experiencing polypharmacy and two focus groups with 14 carers were conducted via Microsoft Teams or telephone and analysed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis. papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Lumbar spine surgery is associated with significant perioperative pain and increased opioid requirements. Objective nociception-guided opioid administration using the surgical pleth index (SPI) may facilitate individualised intraoperative analgesic titration. Dexmedetomidine and subanaesthetic ketamine are commonly used opioid-sparing adjuvants; however, their effects under SPI-guided analgesia remain inadequately studied. papers.abstract: Analytical treatment interruption (ATI) is a closely monitored pause of antiretroviral-therapy (ART) in HIV cure-related research used to assess whether people can maintain viral suppression off ART. We examined HIV-related stigma, disclosure, and support among young women in an ATI-inclusive trial in Durban, South Africa. Nineteen women (age range: 23-32) completed stigma surveys and in-depth-interviews at screening, pre-ATI, post-ATI, and trial-end. We grouped participants by time to restart ART: early (under 16 weeks); delayed (16-44 weeks), and long-term delayed (45-60 weeks). papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Supported Patient Navigation Addressing Social Drivers of Health among Vulnerable Adults in Family Medicine and Geriatrics Safety-Net Clinics
papers.abstract: Health-related social needs such as housing instability, food insecurity, and transportation barriers are associated with worse health outcomes and increased health care utilization, particularly among older adults. Although health systems increasingly screen for these needs, many lack the capacity to provide follow-up support at scale. This pilot evaluation described the implementation and early operational performance of an artificial intelligence-supported, on-demand patient navigation service integrated into an urban safety-net health system. From July 2024 to March 2025, providers placed 149 referrals from family medicine and geriatrics clinics. papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate an early prediction model for perampanel (PER) response in children with epilepsy (CWE) using clinical covariates and ensemble learning, to support individualized treatment decisions. METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 325 CWE (< 15 years) treated with PER from January 2021 to December 2025 was enrolled. papers.title: Programmatic Assessment: Tenets to Remember, Tensions to Resolve, Traps to Avoid, and Tips to Take on Board
papers.abstract: This paper evaluates programmatic assessment (PA) as an educationally coherent framework for medical education, addressing longstanding paradoxes in traditional high stakes models where siloed performance data may fail to capture true learner competence. Programmatic assessment is a comprehensive, programme level strategy that uses multiple low stakes data points over time to inform high stakes progression decisions. While traditional summative assessments provide standardised, objective thresholds essential for national licensing, a growing body of longitudinal evidence indicates that the little and often approach of PA promotes deeper learning and improved retention of clinical skills. papers.title: Feasibility of Privacy-preserving Locally Hosted Language Models for Assessing Medical Student Reflective Writing
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Reflective writing assessment in medical education is labor-intensive and raises data privacy concerns that preclude cloud-based AI solutions. We conducted a feasibility study using a locally-hosted, open-weight large language model (LLM) deployed on institutional servers to assess medical students' reflective writing. The model evaluated 10 de-identified student narratives using two published rubrics across three independent passes, generating rubric-aligned scores and formative feedback. Scores were consistent across passes and rubrics with no statistically significant differences. Expert faculty rated LLM-generated feedback as meeting most quality criteria (mean 5.48/7). These findings support feasibility of a privacy-preserving, locally-hosted LLM for scalable reflective writing assessment. papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: People living with HIV (PLHIV) with ongoing viremia have the potential for onward transmission. Identifying such individuals throughout the care continuum is therefore important for reducing HIV incidence. This study aimed to characterize persons at gaps at different stages of the HIV care continuum in Central Ethiopia. METHODS: PLHIV ≥ 15 years were recruited between 2022 and 2024. papers.abstract: Fetal birth weight (BW) is a critical indicator of the prognosis of perinatal health. Accurate estimation of BW is essential in determining the appropriate delivery method. This single-center study aims to evaluate the performance of various machine learning (ML) algorithms in estimating BW. The study population consisted of 456 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies evaluated at a single tertiary center in the Karaman region of Turkiye between 38 and 41 weeks based on their last menstrual period, who gave birth to a phenotypically normal live newborn within 7 days after the ultrasound examination. papers.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Developing a Future-Ready Nursing Workforce: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming health care through advanced technologies that support clinical practice, education, workforce management, and decision making. As healthcare systems face growing challenges related to workforce shortages, increasing service demands, and rapid digital transformation, there is a need to understand how AI can contribute to the development of a future-ready nursing workforce equipped with the competencies required for modern healthcare environments. AIM: This systematic review aimed to examine the role of AI in developing a future-ready nursing workforce and to synthesize current evidence regarding its applications, benefits, challenges, and implications for workforce preparedness. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring (IONM) reduces neurological risk during major spine surgery. Total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) is generally preferred for IONM; however, the effects of dexmedetomidine and volatile adjuncts on evoked potential (EP) monitoring during propofol-based anesthesia remain inadequately characterized. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The global higher education landscape is undergoing a profound transition due to the convergence of digital technologies and pedagogical theory. In medical education, large language models now demonstrate clinical reasoning capabilities comparable to those of medical students, yet faculty training remains highly inconsistent globally. In Ukraine, this challenge is compounded by wartime pressures and a high rate of «bottom-up» AI adoption (84%) among students, which is often plagued by ethical uncertainty and a lack of structured guidance. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) has gained increasing attention due to its involvement in lipid metabolism and neuroinflammation regulation. High PCSK9 levels are linked to an elevated risk of cerebrovascular events and small vessel diseases. However, systematic research exploring the association between PCSK9 and post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) remains scarce. This study investigated the link between PCSK9 and PSCI. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite substantial progress in the Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission (PMTCT) of HIV in Tanzania, new pediatric HIV infections continue to occur during the postnatal period. Understanding both the incidence of postnatal HIV transmission and contextual factors influencing PMTCT engagement is essential for achieving elimination targets. METHODS: The quantitative component used routinely collected PMTCT data for HIV-exposed infants and their mothers enrolled in PMTCT services in Manyara Region, Tanzania, between January 2019 and October 2023. papers.abstract: We developed a machine learning framework grounded in a computational model of brain function and FDG-PET imaging to predict Alzheimer's disease (AD)-type tau across AD and related disorders (ADRD). The model was trained on 1088 research participants spanning normal aging and ADRD with FDG-PET and flortaucipir-PET (FTP-PET). papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Physicians are increasingly expected to communicate health science to the public, and generative artificial intelligence (AI) makes such content cheap to produce, yet cross-national evidence remains scarce. papers.abstract: The 2021 WHO CNS tumor classification marked a fundamental shift in neuro-oncology: molecular markers rather than histological appearance now define glioma diagnosis and guide treatment. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Pregnancy and the postpartum period can present substantial psychosocial and HIV-care challenges for women living with HIV (WLWH), with potential consequences for psychological well-being, treatment engagement, and maternal and infant health. This study examined whether internalized HIV stigma mediates the relationship between depressive symptoms and antiretroviral therapy (ART) adherence among pregnant and postpartum WLWH in Ghana. Their clinical utility has broadened substantially to include oncology, cardiovascular conditions, transplant monitoring, infectious diseases, and persistent inflammatory disorders. papers.abstract: Women living with HIV (WLWH) in Vietnam face significant structural, social, and interpersonal barriers that hinder their access to care and psychosocial support. While family/partner-based interventions have shown promise globally in improving WLWH health outcomes, few are tailored to the cultural and contextual realities of Vietnam. This study aimed to describe the process of engaging an HIV-focused Community Advisory Board (CAB) in Vietnam to evaluate the contextual fit and feasibility of six evidence-based, family/partner-based interventions for WLWH. Using a community-based participatory research approach, we established a CAB comprising WLWH, their male partners, HIV service providers, and community stakeholders. Interventions were identified through a scoping review and evaluated using the Hexagon Tool across six domains: effectiveness, support, usability, need, fit, and capacity.

papers.title: Work-Life Strain and Emotional Distress: A Comparison of Agriculture/Forestry/Fishing and Construction/ Extraction Workers in California
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Agriculture, Fishing, and Forestry (AFF) and Construction and Extraction (CE) workers experience higher rates of adverse mental health outcomes than workers in other industries. Although several work-related risk factors affecting mental health have been identified in both groups, there is limited understanding of how and why these risks vary between AFF and CE workers. METHODS: Guided by the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) framework, we used data originally from the California Work and Health Survey (CWHS) to investigate the association of known work-life strains and emotional distress among California AFF and CE workers (N = 152). Univariate and bivariate analyses and t-tests were conducted to examine differences in stress, job demands, job control, childcare responsibilities, bullying experiences, and binge drinking between AFF and CE workers in relation to emotional distress.

papers.title: Association of integrated community care and microfinance on mental health outcomes among adults with HIV in Kenya
papers.abstract: We investigated associations between community-based care and microfinance with psychological distress among adults with HIV in Kenya. Using Harambee cluster-randomized trial data, we compared 18-month psychological distress symptom levels between microfinance participants randomized to integrated community-based care (MF+ICB) or usual facility-based care (MF+UC), and non-randomized matched facility-care patients (UC). Psychological distress symptoms were measured by Patient Health Questionnaire-4, Patient Health Questionnaire-2 (depression), and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-2 (anxiety). For within-group change analysis, we used linear mixed models with a random intercept; for between-arm comparisons, we used Poisson regression with cluster-robust errors for risk ratios. papers.title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Model Integrating Chest CT and Cardiac Ultrasound for the Auxiliary Diagnosis of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
papers.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vascular disorder characterized by elevated pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular dysfunction. Conventional imaging modalities, chest computed tomography (CT) and cardiac ultrasound (echocardiography), provide complementary structural and functional information but exhibit incomplete sensitivity and specificity when used alone. This study aimed to evaluate a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model integrating chest CT and cardiac ultrasound for auxiliary PAH diagnosis, benchmarked against right heart catheterization (RHC) as the reference standard. A retrospective observational study was conducted on 100 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 15.2 years; 56% female) with suspected PAH between January 2020 and December 2024. papers.title: A Distributed Vision Transformer-Based Deep Learning Framework for Early Detection and Classification of Lumbar Disc Degeneration
papers.abstract: Lumbar disc degeneration (LDD) is a principal structural cause of chronic low back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the reference modality for assessing the intervertebral discs, but severity grading is performed manually, is limited by inter-observer variability, and becomes a bottleneck as imaging volume grows. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) capture local texture and boundary detail efficiently, yet their restricted receptive field limits the modeling of relationships extending across several vertebral levels, whereas Vision Transformers (ViTs) represent such global context through self-attention. papers.title: Scalable classification of infant breast milk feeding status from clinical notes using weak supervision and rule-based natural language processing
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Extract infant breast milk feeding status from electronic health record clinical notes to support observational drug-safety studies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Infant notes (19 489; 228 infants) were weakly labeled by large language model (LLM) and validated on 1045 manually reviewed notes. papers.title: Designing an AI-resistant assignment: Can we safeguard against student use of artificial intelligence?
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots and large language models (LLMs) have the potential to revolutionize higher education by providing personalized learning, enhancing accessibility, and offering real-time academic support. However, ChatGPT and similar smart text-generating LLMs can be easily exploited by students to write assignments or essays, challenging traditional methods of assessment. For third-year students in the dental hygiene program at a Canadian university, a written assignment was designed by incorporating several features to prevent students from exploiting AI in their writing. A study was conducted to explore students' use of AI tools in assignment writing. papers.title: A questionnaire-based model to prioritize additional support during HIV testing encounters among men who have sex with men: temporal and geographic external validation
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: HIV sentinel surveillance collects behavioral and service-use information from men who have sex with men (MSM), but these data are mainly used for routine reporting. We assessed whether pre-test questionnaire data could help prioritize testing encounters for optional additional support. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective prediction modeling study using de-identified MSM surveillance records. Data from Nantong collected in 2020-2023 were used for model development, and records from 2024-2025 were used for temporal validation. Surveillance records from an external city in Shandong Province were used for geographic external validation. Immune-checkpoint blockade and candidate predictive biomarkers in HIV-negative Kaposi sarcoma: current evidence and a practical research framework
papers.abstract: Kaposi sarcoma (KS) is a KSHV/HHV-8-driven vascular neoplasm with heterogeneous HIV-negative epidemiological settings. Immune-checkpoint blockade is biologically plausible, but direct clinical evidence remains limited to a small, non-comparative phase II cohort of pembrolizumab in classic or endemic KS. Its 71% best objective response rate is a signal that warrants confirmation, not comparative evidence or a basis for biomarker-guided treatment. This narrative review distinguishes established clinical observations from candidate translational hypotheses, appraises analytical and biological limitations of proposed markers, and outlines requirements for prospective subtype-stratified validation. PD-L1 expression, tumor mutational burden, and KSHV DNA should not be used as stand-alone selection or exclusion tests in routine care.

papers.title: Pilot Mixed-Methods Evaluation of Simulation-Based Focused Cardiac Ultrasound Teaching for Final-Year Medical Students
papers.abstract: Background Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used within emergency and acute care, yet undergraduate exposure to focused bedside echocardiography remains variable. Simulation may provide an opportunity for students to develop practical ultrasound skills while integrating findings into clinical assessment and decision-making. This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of a simulation-based bedside echocardiography teaching programme for final-year medical students and explored differences in confidence and knowledge between pre- and post-session respondents. Methodology A mixed-methods educational evaluation was undertaken with final-year medical students during their Preparation for Practice placement at a UK teaching hospital. papers.title: Evaluating RAG Configurations for Clinical Information Extraction from EHR Notes: Aged Care Case Study
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Clinical information extraction from unstructured electronic health records is important for supporting clinical decision making and healthcare research. However, large language models can struggle to accurately extract domain-specific information without effective adaptation. Retrieval-augmented generation offers a promising approach, but the optimal configuration for clinical information extraction remains unclear. This study evaluated different retrieval-augmented generation configurations for extracting frailty index items, malnutrition risk factors, and agitation in dementia from clinical notes collected from 40 Australian residential aged care facilities. papers.title: Performance of PIM, PRISM, and PELOD scores in a resource-limited North Indian paediatric intensive care unit
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric mortality prediction models are widely used in high-income nations but remain under-validated in resource-limited settings with different disease profiles and care resources. This study evaluated the performance of pediatric risk of mortality score III (PRISM-III), pediatric index of mortality-3 (PIM-3), and pediatric logistic organ dysfunction score-2 (PELOD-2) in predicting mortality in a resource limited paediatric intensive care unit. AIM: To determine the discriminative ability and calibration of PRISM III, PIM-3, and PELOD-2 for predicting 30-day mortality. METHODS: This was an observational study over 15 months and included 175 children aged 1 month to 18 years. papers.title: Toward Fairness in Machine Learning Models for Predicting Treatment Retention and Premature Discontinuation in Medication for Opioid Use Disorder
papers.abstract: Persistent low retention and completion rates in medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) have driven the use of machine learning (ML) models to predict retention and identify patients at risk of premature discontinuation. However, the fairness of these models across patient populations remains largely unexplored, raising concerns about their application in treatment decision support. This study systematically assesses algorithmic fairness in ML models for predicting MOUD retention and premature discontinuation and investigates the effectiveness of bias mitigation techniques. papers.title: Immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine in adults living with HIV compared with HIV-uninfected adults: a study from China
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) in adults aged ≥18 years living with HIV and to provide evidence supporting influenza vaccination in this population in China. METHODS: This single-center, open-label comparative analysis was derived from a larger three-arm clinical study. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its relationship with coronary artery disease (CAD) remains uncertain. METHODS: This systematic review included observational studies reporting adjusted effect estimates for CAD outcomes among HCV-infected and HCV-uninfected adults. Adjusted hazard ratios, risk ratios, and odds ratios were combined on the logarithmic scale using a random-effects model and are presented as a summary relative association estimate with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). papers.title: Interleukin pathway genotype and the grandiosity dimension of psychosis: a machine learning gene set analysis with unsupervised anomaly detection controls
papers.abstract: Immune involvement in psychosis is well supported, although most of the evidence comes from studies of negative and deficit symptoms. Grandiosity, in comparison, has received little attention. It is, however, the one symptom for which the two main accounts of inflammation in psychosis, activation and reward blunting, make opposite predictions. papers.title: Interpretable machine learning identifies predictors of IGF-1 during growth hormone therapy in boys
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) is widely used to guide growth hormone (GH) therapy, yet its predictors during the maintenance phase and puberty remain incompletely understood. We aimed to predict IGF-1 standard deviation scores (SDS) at 3 and 12 months in GH-treated boys and to identify key predictors of IGF-1 dynamics using interpretable modeling approaches. METHODS: Data from 72 boys with growth hormone deficiency or idiopathic short stature from a previous Swedish clinical trial were analyzed using early-life characteristics, GH treatment variables, and puberty-related measures. Linear regression, Elastic Net regression, and explainable boosting machine (EBM) models were evaluated with nested five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation. papers.title: An attention-guided dense convolutional network for automated diabetic foot ulcer segmentation
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: A large number of diabetic patients have diabetic foot ulcers (DFU), and it is essential to segment the regions of the ulcer in a timely and accurate manner to treat them. The segmentation task is very difficult due to the highly irregular shape of the ulcers and very small areas of lesions, up to 0.04% of the DFU image. METHODS: We aim to develop an attention-guided dense convolutional network, called UlcerNet, which is able to extract fine-grained ulcer features at different scales. papers.abstract: This study investigates intracellular (IC) exposure of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) and its clinical determinants in experienced people living with HIV. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The global prevalence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) continues to rise, and GDM significantly increases the risk of spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB), posing serious threats to maternal and neonatal health. Existing models for assessing sPTB risk in patients with GDM remain limited in accuracy, nonlinear relationship capture, and the handling of complex feature interactions. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the performance differences between eight individual machine learning algorithms and a Stacking ensemble learning architecture, and to achieve risk identification and stratification through optimized model-building strategies. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate registration between cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images and intraoral scans is fundamental to digital implant planning because registration errors may propagate throughout the digital workflow and affect the accuracy of computer-guided implant surgery. Conventional point-based registration relies on manually selected anatomical landmarks and may be compromised by metallic artifacts that obscure dental structures. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted registration has recently emerged as a promising alternative; however, evidence comparing its performance with conventional point-based registration under clinically challenging conditions remains limited. papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Seasonal variations in intraocular pressure (IOP) are reported in glaucoma, but differences between subtypes and the influence of filtration surgery remain unclear. papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections account for more than a million deaths each year, yet this burden remains largely invisible-most fatalities are recorded under the underlying diagnosis of HIV or haematological malignancy rather than the fungal disease itself. papers.abstract: Background: Antimicrobial resistance is a growing concern in long-term care facilities (LTCs), where residents are often older, have chronic health conditions, and are frequently prescribed antimicrobials. Historically, antimicrobial resistance data from Canadian LTCs have been limited. This study explores the use of lab-based surveillance data from the Public Health Agency of Canada's AMRNet program to describe antimicrobial resistance in LTCs. papers.abstract: Background. Care management programs increasingly rely on prediction algorithms to decide which patients receive limited healthcare resources. Objective. To evaluate how three modifiable design choices (selection threshold, feature set, and training objective) affect allocation equity in care management targeting. Methods. papers.abstract: Background: Ultrasound is commonly used to assess hepatosplenic morbidity in schistosomiasis, but access may be limited in resource-constrained settings. Abdominal palpation is simple and inexpensive, yet its clinical value and diagnostic performance for detecting ultrasound-defined organ enlargement remains uncertain. papers.abstract: Background: Empirical evidence on the health impacts of brownfield land (previously developed land that may be contaminated) remains limited, mainly due to poorly defined exposures and pathways. papers.title: Survey of Physician Attitudes on Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Objective To better understand how physicians view the potential use of artificial intelligence (AI) in their practices. Method We conducted an online cross-sectional survey of 1,258 physicians (MD, DO, MBBS or equivalent) in the United States (US) and Canada from December 2023 through February 2026. The survey contained 34 questions focused on 6 areas: (1) demographics, (2) training, (3) clinical benefits, (4) clinical concerns, (5) clinical AI prediction tools, and (6) generative AI. Results A total of 130 completed surveys were received (response rate, 10%). Top specialties included psychiatry (46.2%), internal medicine (14.6%) and pediatrics (13.8%). A total of 16.9% had training in computer science or information technology and 40.8% in statistics. Nearly half (46.9%) had no formal training in AI and were self-taught. Those with training in AI received it through vendors or at work.

papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) screening increasingly relies on machine learning models trained on the AQ-10 and Q-CHAT questionnaire datasets, and these models are widely reported to reach 95 to 99 percent accuracy, so confirming whether that accuracy reflects genuine diagnostic learning is vital. This paper examines whether that accuracy reflects genuine diagnostic learning or is simply an artifact of how the datasets are built. papers.abstract: Surveys can reach large samples but capture only pre-defined answers, with identical responses often concealing very different reasoning. We tested whether AI-moderated interviews capture this reasoning at scale. papers.abstract: Background. Canada's loss of measles elimination status in 2025 highlighted the vulnerability of populations with concentrated immunity gaps. We quantified these differences across five provincial measles waves in 2025-2026. Methods. papers.abstract: Background: Depression/anxiety symptoms emerge early in life. We examined emotional symptom trajectories, from early childhood, in three UK birth-cohorts spanning successive generations and diverse socio-ethnic contexts. papers.title: Target Trial Emulation of Metformin for Dementia Prevention in All of Us: Robustness to Cohort and Confounder Definitions
papers.abstract: Metformin use has been associated with a lower risk of incident dementia than other antidiabetics. We perform target trial emulation and causal competing risk analysis in the NIH All of Us (AoU) Research Program database, contrasting the effects of metformin and sulfonylurea initiation on dementia onset and death without dementia. papers.title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
papers.abstract: Increased computing power has transformed computational science and improved predictive capabilities for complex systems, but many phenomena still exceed current simulation capabilities or require rapid evaluations for fast design iterations. Closure models address this challenge by approximating unresolved effects in reduced or incomplete dynamical systems. Data-driven closures offer a flexible mechanism for improving model accuracy and applicability, but approaches that embed the closure within a computational model for construction and training phases can be computationally expensive and cause numerical instabilities in the computational model during training. papers.title: PlantVLM-Edge: Quantized Vision-Language Models for On-Device Crop Health Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is essential for sustainable agricultural production, yet accurate diagnosis often requires expert knowledge that is not readily available. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, and natural-language interaction, creating new opportunities for intelligent crop health assessment. However, deploying VLMs on resource-constrained devices remains challenging due to their substantial computational and memory requirements. This paper presents PlantVLM-Edge, a quantized vision-language framework for conversational crop health diagnosis that can run entirely on resource-constrained edge devices. papers.title: DistDebug-Bench: Can LLM Agents Diagnose Bugs in Distributed Systems?
papers.abstract: LLM agents show strong potential in software engineering tasks such as competitive programming and code synthesis. Existing benchmarks, however, largely focus on small-scale settings such as self-contained Python modules, leaving distributed systems, an essential class of production software, under-examined. We introduce DistDebug-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating agents' ability to diagnose complex-system failures at the code level. It curates 120 high-quality real-world bugs from 11 widely used distributed systems, spanning 5 programming languages and 10 failure patterns. Through an extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs and agents, we identify substantial gaps between current agents and real-world debugging tasks. papers.title: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records
papers.abstract: Suicide prevention remains a critical public health challenge, and electronic health records (EHRs) provide an opportunity to characterize suicide-related risk indicators using documented clinical, behavioral, medical, and social-contextual information. This paper presents a multidimensional machine learning framework to model and estimate suicide-related outcomes using MIMIC-IV EHR data. We construct clinically motivated diagnosis categories and define a composite outcome from documented codes corresponding to suicidal ideation, suicide attempt, prior suicidal behavior, and intentional self-harm. papers.abstract: We introduce the Poisson Super Learner, a scalable ensemble method for survival and competing risks prediction with right-censored data. papers.abstract: Battery degradation remains a central challenge in the development and broad application of sustainable energy technologies. Accurate degradation prediction is challenging, as battery aging emerges from complex and heterogeneous interactions among cycling behavior, operating conditions, and cell chemistry. papers.abstract: An experimental agent can succeed for the wrong reasons. Evaluations, however, often focus on the outcome, not the experiments, evidence, and inferences that produced it. Agents learn unknown regulatory systems through budgeted experimentation, then predict unseen interventions, diagnose hidden faults, and attempt rescues. papers.abstract: Time-series segmentation, studied as either Change Point Detection (CPD) or State Detection (SD), underpins a broad range of monitoring and diagnostic applications. However, the field suffers from a persistent divide between the statistical community (focusing on CPD) and the machine learning and data mining communities (focusing on SD). Consequently, the literature remains fragmented: evaluations typically cover narrow methodological families, datasets are often small or homogeneous, and CPD and SD are rarely evaluated together. papers.abstract: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) have recently been proposed as a promising alternative to Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs). However, empirical evaluations on structured medical datasets remain scarce, and commonly reported metrics like AUROC can yield overly optimistic performance estimates on imbalanced clinical cohorts. papers.abstract: Large language model agents increasingly take consequential actions in digital and physical environments, where safety risks may emerge only after multiple interaction steps. This has motivated world-model-driven predictive safety guardrails, which anticipate future consequences before execution. However, existing evaluations largely focus on end-to-end safety outcomes, leaving unclear whether safety gains arise from reliable prediction and faithful use of predicted risks. papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are characterized by their progressive nature, with distinct stages that require precise identification and tracking of progression trajectories for accurate diagnosis. However, existing diagnostic methods often fail to fully capture the unique brain patterns associated with different stages, limiting their ability to effectively target specific stages of the disorders. To address this issue, we propose a Stage-aware Multimodal Brain Graph Contrastive Learning (smBGC) method. papers.abstract: Automated liver ultrasound report generation improves the diagnosis of liver diseases by producing clinically structured descriptions of anatomical and disease-related findings. papers.abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but with limited labeled data. papers.abstract: Language models with similar benchmark accuracy can succeed on different items. Overall scores do not show where their performance differs or which item properties might explain those differences. papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to answer questions over financial filings, where an unfaithful answer can mislead investment, compliance, or client decisions. papers.abstract: Accurate diabetes prediction is critical for early clinical intervention, yet existing machine-learning pipelines often fail due to class imbalance, noisy physiological measurements, and redundant or weakly informative features. papers.abstract: Machine learning models deployed in decision-making pipelines, from vehicle routing to dynamic pricing to clinical decision support, must remain reliable in the face of low-quality training data. papers.abstract: Clinical interpretation of a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) often requires answering targeted diagnostic questions with clear, quantifiable decisions. papers.abstract: The spatial intelligence of large vision-language models (LVLMs) requires the ability to combine local visual observations into a geometrically consistent representation of the physical world. Many static benchmarks assess isolated spatial judgments, such as relative direction or distance, while interactive embodied evaluations combine perception with exploration, planning, control, and simulator-specific execution. papers.abstract: Surgical video understanding is essential for intraoperative assistance such as workflow monitoring, instrument preparation and procedural documentation. papers.abstract: Data-driven sequential decision making in marketing and healthcare can benefit from observations collected in related environments, particularly when data in the environment of interest are limited. papers.abstract: This paper presents a privacy-preserving mood monitoring framework that classifies emotional states from ECG-derived heart rate variability (HRV) features. papers.title: Steer, Don't Tell: Breaking Reasoning Plateaus with Reachability-Aligned Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Post training for large reasoning models remains insufficient on challenging problems, whose correct trajectories are hard to sample. Though prior works address this difficulty by integrating supervised fine tuning on expert trajectories with reinforcement learning, such external experts are not always available. Existing self improvement methods instead use reference solutions to create a privileged self-teacher. Yet privileged teacher correctness does not imply student reachability. Solution conditioning shifts the teacher distribution toward actions unlikely under the unprivileged student, producing seemingly "correct" trajectories that are unreachable or even mal-formed learning targets. papers.title: FastAgent: A Physics-Aware FastFluent-to-Fluent Workflow for Rapid CFD Screening and Industrial Steam Dewaxing Design
papers.abstract: Industrial computational fluid dynamics (CFD) becomes costly when complex geometries, long transients and coupled physics must be evaluated across large design spaces. We introduce FastAgent, a physics-aware campaign controller built around FastFluent, a lightweight numerical engine for rapid physical screening. FastFluent supplies stage-specific fields and diagnostics; FastAgent allocates physical models, numerical resolution and simulation horizons by the active quantities of interest (QoIs), while returned Fluent discrepancies update subsequent decisions. Across six public CFD benchmark campaigns, the framework reduces normalised worst-QoI error by 5.68-99.14% and accelerates decision-relevant computation by factors of 1.53-15.36 relative to a matched Generic Agent control. papers.title: Conversational Interaction for LLM-Based Clinical Text-to-SQL: A User Study with Healthcare Professionals
papers.abstract: Conversational text-to-SQL interfaces could give healthcare professionals natural-language access to electronic health record (EHR) data, but evidence for their real-world usability remains limited: prior evaluations have relied largely on curated benchmarks with fully specified questions or on simulated users. We report a user study in which 14 physicians who regularly work with EHR data used both a single-turn and a conversational multi-turn text-to-SQL interface over the MIMIC-IV database in a within-subjects design; dialogue analyses additionally drew on interaction logs from 21 healthcare professionals across the main study and two pilot studies. papers.title: Where Causal Discovery Breaks on Real Data: Measuring the Assumptions One Property at a Time
papers.abstract: Causal discovery is usually evaluated on simulators or on systems whose ground truth follows from physics or design. When it fails on other real data, the failure is attributed to assumptions that may not hold, but which ones fail, and by how much, is rarely measured. We measure the observable properties of the data they bear on, one property at a time, on a real panel. The case study follows 2,901 US public firms over 31 quarters, with 71 types of corporate action from SEC 8-K filings, 11 financial-statement items, and an expert graph over 651 action-state pairs. The panel breaks measurable requirements of discovery: tails that survive winsorisation, balance-sheet items and revenue close to random walks, and interventions too rare to detect effects of a tenth of a standard deviation in 40 of 71 actions.
